obzhaya-informatsiya.title: General information
obzhaya-informatsiya.html:
Terms and definitions

  • System - the CloudPayments payment gateway.

  • Merchant - a business that uses the system.

  • API - a software interface for interacting with a system through https://api.cloudpayments.ru.

  • Dashboard - the merchant space in the system, available at https://merchant.cloudpayments.ru.

  • Card - a bank card issued by the Visa, Mastercard, or Mir payment system.

  • Acquirer - the settlement bank.

  • Issuer - the bank that issued the card.

  • Holder - a person to whom the issuer has issued a card for use.

  • Widget - a payment form provided by the system for the cardholder to enter card details and complete authorization.

  • 3D Secure - a protocol for verifying the cardholder's identity with the issuer.

Operation types

The system involves two types of transactions: payment and refund.

  • When the payment is made, the funds are transferred from the holder's account to the merchant. For a refund, the funds are transferred the other way around.

  • The merchant issues a refund if the customer wants to return the product.

  • The refund is always linked to a payment transaction, the amount of which is returned to the cardholder. Both the full payment and part of it can be refunded. The funds are usually returned to the cardholder's card on the same day, but sometimes, depending on the issuing bank, this can take up to 3 days.

  • Unlike a refund, a payment transaction can be canceled.

  • The merchant cancels a payment if it was made by mistake, for example, due to an incorrect amount or technical failure. There is one limitation: the transaction can only be canceled when using a two-stage payment scheme. At the same time, the funds will be released on the cardholder’s card almost instantly.

Payment processing methods

There are two ways to process payments: single-stage and two-stage, also known as the single message system (SMS) and dual message system (DMS), respectively.

Single-stage payment is processed with a single command, which authorizes and subsequently debits the funds to the merchant.

Two-stage payment uses two separate commands: one for authorization and one for charging the funds. After successful authorization, the transaction amount is held on the cardholder's account, so they cannot use the funds. Next, the merchant has up to 7 days, depending on the card type, to confirm the transaction, after which the funds are debited. If the operation is not confirmed within this period, it will be canceled automatically. You can confirm either full authorization amount or part of it.

As a rule, a two-stage method is used to collect a deposit from the payer, for example, by rental companies or hotels.

Depending on the configuration, the system can automatically confirm two-stage payments after the specified number of days.

Payment methods

Payment can be made in the following ways:

  • Through the payment form, the widget. You add a script to your website that opens a secure payment form, an iframe for entering card details.

  • Via the API using a card cryptogram. A checkout script is integrated into your website to collect card details from any form, encrypt and generate a cryptogram for secure server-to-server transmission.

  • Via the SDK for mobile apps. The mobile SDK is integrated into your iOS or Android app to accept card payments directly from your customers' smartphones or tablets.

  • Via the API using a card token: recurring payments. Following the first payment via the widget or by cryptogram, the system assigns a token to the card details. The token can be safely stored and used for merchant-initiated payments (one-click payments). The token is returned in the Pay notification and in the API response

  • Via a configured recurring payment plan. Following the first payment or a one-ruble authorization for card verification, a token is assigned to the card details. This token is then used to create a subscription plan for recurring payments. Payments are processed automatically by the system without the payer's confirmation. These payments follow a configured schedule, which can be set to once a day (or every few days), once a week (or every few weeks) or once a month (or every few months). If a scheduled payment attempt fails, a notification is sent, and the attempt is retried within a day. After three consecutive failed attempts, the subscription is automatically canceled. When creating a plan, a maximum number of billing cycles can be specified (for example, 12 months for a monthly subscription), after which the subscription will automatically terminate.

  • Customizable payment acceptance forms. Payment forms allow foundations and other organizations to accept donations directly to their accounts using a configurable, customizable payment form. This form can be shared as a link c.cloudpayments.ru/payments/ or as a QR code, which can be placed in both online broadcasts and offline marketing materials (flyers, brochures, etc.). The form makes it much easier to accept donations. In the new "Payment forms" section of the dashboard, you can create and customize up to 5 payment forms. The link and QR code for sending to payers become available once the form is saved.

3D Secure.

3D Secure is the collective name for the security programs developed by Visa and Mastercard. The purpose of the program is to verify the identity of the cardholder, allowing the issuer to protect against unauthorized card use prior to payment. In practice, it works as follows: the cardholder enters their card details and is then redirected to the issuer's website to enter a password or verification code. Typically, the code is sent via SMS. If the code is entered correctly, the payment is processed. Otherwise, it is declined.

3D Secure is not triggered for all cards during checkout, but only for those whose issuing banks support the technology. Processing payments without 3D Secure is a less secure option.

platezhniy-widget.title: Payment widget
platezhniy-widget.html:
Payment widget is a pop-up form used to enter the payer's card details and email address. The widget automatically determines the type of payment network: Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, or Mir, as well as the issuing bank, and displays the corresponding logos. The form is optimized for all browsers and mobile devices. Inside the widget, an iframe opens that ensures the secure transmission of card details and does not require compliance certification from the merchant. _Widget

Detailed developer documentation: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/docs/widget.html

Demo of the payment form builder: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/app/demo

Demo widget

A demonstration of how the Widget works is available in our demo store:

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited.


Widget installation

To install the widget, add the script to the head section of your website:

javascript
<script src="https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/bundles/cloudpayments.js"></script>

Warning: Use cloudpayments.js to maintain PCI compliance by ensuring that payment details are sent directly to CloudPayments without affecting your server. Always load cloudpayments.js from https://widget.cloudpayments.ru to remain compliant. Do not bundle the script or host it yourself. _Widget

To display the payment form, register a function to call the pay method by passing either the auth or the charge parameter to it:

json
this.pay = function () {
 var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    widget.pay('auth', // or 'charge'
        { //options
            publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000002', // ID from the dashboard
            description: 'Payment for goods at example.com', // Payment description
            amount: 100, // Amount
            currency: 'RUB', // Currency
            accountId: 'user@example.com', // Payer ID (optional)
            invoiceId: '1234567', // Order number (optional)
            email: 'user@example.com', // Payer email (optional)
            skin: "mini", // Widget design (optional)
            autoClose: 3, // Time in seconds before widget auto-close (optional)
            data: {
                myProp: 'myProp value'
            },
            configuration: {
                common: {
                    successRedirectUrl: "https://{your website}/success", // Redirection URL
                    failRedirectUrl: "https://{your website}/fail"        // If paid via T-Pay
                }
            },
            payer: {
                firstName: 'Test',
                lastName: 'Testov',
                middleName: 'Testovich',
                birth: '1955-02-24',
                address: 'test drive test home',
                street: 'Lenina',
                city: 'MO',
                country: 'RU',
                phone: '+71234567890',
                postcode: '345'
            }
        },
        {
            onSuccess: function (options) { // Success
                // Triggered on payment success
            },
            onFail: function (reason, options) { // Fail
                // Triggered on payment failure
            },
            onComplete: function (paymentResult, options) {
                // Triggered as soon as the widget receives a response
                // with transaction result from api.cloudpayments
                // For example, calling your analytics
            }
        }
    )
};

Then, call the function in response to an event, such as clicking the Pay button:

javascript
$('#checkout').click(pay);

Notice: The example uses the jQuery library.

A demonstration of how the widget works is available in our demo store:
https://show.cloudpayments.ru

Example of running the widget without jQuery:

javascript
document.querySelector('#checkout').onclick = pay

Embedded JSFiddle:

json
<script async src="//jsfiddle.net/tretyakovsky/xvec6jpb/35/embed/js,html/dark/"></script>

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited. _Widget

Parameters

Notice: According to the NSPK requirements, merchant platforms providing telecommunication services (MCC 4814 Telecommunication Services), must provide the payer's phone number. If the phone number is missing from the request, acquiring banks will decline the transactions.

The phone number must be passed in the Phone parameter within the Payer object.

Format: digits only, without delimiters such as hyphens or parentheses.

Example: +71234567890 _Widget

Calling the pay function with either the auth or the charge argument determines the payment processing method:

  • charge for single-stage payments

  • auth for two-stage payments

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

publicId

string

Yes

Website ID, can be found in the dashboard

amount

float

Yes

Payment amount

currency

string

Yes

Currency: RUB/USD/EUR/GBP

accountId

string

Required for subscription creation

User ID

description

string

No

Free-form description of the payment purpose

invoiceId

string

No

Order or invoice number

email

string

No

User's email

requireEmail

bool

No

Requirement to display the user email address field in the widget

data

JSON

No

Any other data associated with the transaction, including instructions for creating a subscription or generating an online receipt, must be wrapped in the cloudpayments object. Reserved parameter names: name, firstName, middleName, lastName, nick, phone, address, comment, birthDate

skin

string

No

Widget design selection. Possible options: classic, modern, mini. Default is classic

retryPayment

bool

No

Displays the "Retry payment" button upon a failed transaction. Default is true

autoClose

number

No

Automatically closes the widget after successful payment following a specified number of seconds, from 3 to 10

payer

object

No

Additional field used to pass payer information: firstName, lastName, middleName, birth, street, address, city, country, phone, postcode

configuration.common.successRedirectUrl

string

No

Redirect URL after a successful non-card payment. For SBP, the value must not exceed 1024 characters, use ASCII encoding, and comply with RFC-3986

configuration.common.failRedirectUrl

string

No

Redirect URL after a failed T-Pay payment

disableEmail

bool

No

Allows hiding the email address field. To hide it, omit requireEmail or set it to false

You can configure the form's behavior for successful or failed payments using the following parameters:

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

onSuccess

Function or String

No

Specify either a function or a website URL. If a function is specified, it will be called after the payment is successfully completed and the user closes the widget. If a URL is specified, the user will be redirected to that page

onFail

Function or String

No

Specify either a function or a website URL. If a function is specified, it will be called after a failed payment. If a URL is specified, the user will be redirected to that page

onComplete

Function

No

Specify a function to be triggered as soon as the widget receives the transaction result response. Redirects are not allowed in this method

Widget language settings

By default, the widget is displayed in Russian. To display the widget in another language, pass the language parameter in the widget initialization settings.

javascript
var widget = new cp.CloudPayments({language: "en-US"});

List of supported languages:

Language

Timezone

Code

Russian

MSK

ru-RU

English

CET

en-US

Kazakh

ALMT

kk-KZ

Recurring payments (subscriptions)

After the payment is successfully completed, the widget can automatically create a subscription for recurring payments. To do this, add several initialization parameters:

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

Interval

string

Yes

Interval. Possible values: Day, Week, Month

Period

int

Yes

Period. Combined with interval, 1 Month is once a month, and 2 Week is once every two weeks. Must be greater than 0

MaxPeriods

int

No

Maximum number of payments in subscription. By default, no restrictions. If you specify a number, make sure it is greater than 0

Amount

number

No

Recurring payment amount. By default, this matches the initial payment amount. If specifying a custom amount, ensure it is greater than 0

StartDate

DateTime

No

Date and time of the first recurring payment. By default, the next payment will occur after the specified interval and period. If specifying a custom date, ensure it is set in the future

CustomerReceipt

string

No

Data for online receipts generation in recurring payments

The parameters for launching recurring payments must be added to the data.CloudPayments.recurrent object, as shown in the example below:

json
this.pay = function () {
    var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    var receipt = {
        Items: [// Receipt items
            {
                label: 'Product name 3', // Product name
                price: 300.00, // Cost
                quantity: 3.00, // Quantity
                amount: 900.00, // Amount
                vat: 20, // VAT rate
                method: 0, // Tag 1214: payment method flag
                object: 0, // Tag 1212: payment subject flag
            }
        ],
        taxationSystem: 0,
        email: 'user@example.com',
        phone: '+71234567890',
        isBso: false,
        amounts: {
            electronic: 900.00,
            advancePayment: 0.00,
            credit: 0.00,
            provision: 0.00
        }
    };

    var data = {};
    data.CloudPayments = {
        CustomerReceipt: receipt,
        recurrent: {
            interval: 'Month',
            period: 1,
            customerReceipt: receipt
        }
    };

    widget.charge({
        publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000001',
        description: 'Monthly subscription for access to example.com',
        amount: 1000,
        currency: 'RUB',
        invoiceId: '1234567',
        accountId: 'user@example.com',
        data: data
    },
    function (options) {
        // Triggered on payment success
    },
    function (reason, options) {
        // Triggered on payment failure
    });
};

Please note that you can create a subscription by specifying the accountId parameter, which can be an email address, a phone number, or any other payer ID.

For more examples of creating recurring payments from the widget, see the Integration scenarios.

To cancel recurring payments, use the merchant dashboard, the API, or provide the customer with a link to the system's website:

https://my.cloudpayments.ru/

There they can find and cancel their subscriptions independently. _Widget

Mobile widget

The script automatically identifies the user's device and launches the most appropriate widget: desktop or mobile. For the convenience of customers, the mobile version of the widget opens in full screen, allowing them to pay either by card or via one of the alternative payment methods.

platezhniy-konstructor.title: Payment form builder
platezhniy-konstructor.html:
PaymentBlocks is a block builder for creating custom payment forms. You can make your own form design.

The form is optimized for use in any browser and on any mobile device. Inside the block, an iframe opens that ensures the secure transmission of card details and does not require compliance certification from the merchant.

The form supports all payment methods available in CloudPayments. _Payment Blocks

Warning: The payment amount must be verified independently. To verify the amount, you can use the following notifications: Check to verify the amount before payment, and Pay to verify the amount after payment.

Builder demo

A demonstration of how the Builder works is available via this link: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/app/demo

You can use either test card data or real card data for testing. No funds will be debited.

Differences from the widget

Key differences

Widget

Payment form builder

Display method

Pop-up window

Embedded on the page. Can be placed directly on the order page

Customization

2 modes: modern (dark theme), classic (light theme)

Full customization support

Can be closed by the customer

Yes

No

Displays payment amount and purpose

Yes

No

Can update payment data

No

You can adjust the payment to reflect changes in the cart

Supports forced unmount

No

Yes, via blocksApp.unmount()

Install the payment form builder

To install the builder, add the script to the head section of your website:

javascript
<script src="https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/bundles/paymentblocks.js"></script>

Next, create a DOM element to mount the builder to:

javascript
<div id="element"></div>

Then declare the payment form builder. The parameters are described in more detail below:

javascript
var blocksApp = new cp.PaymentBlocks(
    initializationParams, // Initialization parameters. Required for the builder to work
    customizationParams // Customization parameters. Optional
);

And mount it to the DOM element you created:

javascript
blocksApp.mount(document.getElementById("element"));

Remove the builder from DOM

You can remove the payment form builder from the DOM element at any time:

javascript
blocksApp.unmount();

Events (callbacks)

It's possible to receive event notifications and handle them, which requires adding handlers for the corresponding events.

To do this, you need to add the following block, or part of it, after mounting:

javascript
blocksApp.on("destroy", () => { // Subscribe to the payment error event
     console.log("destroy");
});

blocksApp.on("success", (result) => { // Subscribe to the successful payment result event
     console.log("success", result);
});

blocksApp.on("fail", (result) => { // Subscribe to the builder destruction event
     console.log("fail", result);
});

Callback types

Callback

Trigger conditions

Callback initialization code

Result examples

destroy

Destroying the payment block through unmount()

Not applicable

{ "type": "payment", "data": { "transactionId": 4581867878, "ReasonCode": 5206 }, "message": 3D Secure authentication failed", "status": "fail"}

Unsubscribe

You can also unsubscribe from events:

javascript
// Unsubscribe from successful payment result events
blocksApp.off("success");

// Unsubscribe from payment error events
blocksApp.off("fail");

// Unsubscribe from builder destruction events
blocksApp.off("destroy");

script-checkout.title: Checkout script
script-checkout.html:
Checkout is a script embedded into your website that collects card details from a specified form and uses them to generate a cryptogram for payment processing via our API.

The cryptogram is generated using the RSA algorithm with a 2048-bit key length and meets the standard for card data protection. If the requirements described below are followed, card details will not be accessible to you, but your server still impacts their security.

Demo checkout

A demonstration of the Checkout script is available in our demo store: https://show.cloudpayments.ru/checkout/

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited.


Requirements

Form requirements

  • Must operate over an HTTPS connection with a valid SSL certificate.

  • Form fields must not contain the name attribute, this prevents card details from reaching the server when the form is sent.

  • The field for entering the card number must support entry of 16 to 19 digits.

Cryptogram requirements

  • Must be generated exclusively by the original checkout script loaded from the system's official addresses.

  • The cryptogram must not be stored after the payment is made or reused for subsequent transactions.

PCI DSS security requirements

From the PCI DSS perspective, this type of connection is classified as "E-commerce merchants who outsource all payment processing to PCI DSS validated third parties, and who have a website(s) that doesn’t directly receive cardholder data but that can impact the security of the payment transaction. No electronic storage, processing, or transmission of any cardholder data on the merchant’s systems or premises,", meaning that while payment data processing is handled by a third party, your website still impacts the security of card details.

javascript

});

    cardNumber: '4242 4242 4242 4242',

    expDateYear: '24',

recurrentniye-platezhi.title: Recurring payments
recurrentniye-platezhi.html:
Recurring payments, also known as subscription payments or automated payments, let you charge the customer's bank card regularly without requiring the payer to re-enter card details or initiate each payment.

Recurring payments always start with the initial payment, for which the payer must enter the details of his card. For subsequent recurring payments, you must familiarize the cardholder with the billing schedule and obtain their consent for direct debiting.

There is a common belief that recurring billing simply boils down to setting an amount to be charged to the customer's card each month. Consequently, the choice of a recurring payment provider is often based solely on the cost of the services. In reality, the process is more complex, because quality service requires far more features and capabilities. We have done everything to make launching and processing recurring payments in CloudPayments as simple and flexible as possible.

Start and stop recurring payments

Recurring payments can be started at any time after the initial payment: immediately, one week later, or one month later. There is only one restriction: the interval between recurring payments, as well as between the initial payment and the first recurring payment, cannot exceed one year.

Example: the customer pays for the first month of service through an initial payment and agrees to monthly debiting from their card starting from the second month.

Recurring payments can be started via API or payment widget.

If the customer cancels further payments, you can terminate the subscription at any time:

  • From the dashboard: https://merchant.cloudpayments.ru/login

  • Via the API

Additionally, the payer can independently find and cancel their recurring payments on the CloudPayments website:
https://my.cloudpayments.ru/ru/unsubscribe

Payment schedule customization

Select the billing period and interval

The system can make recurring payments every 2 weeks, once a month, every 3 months, and so on: you can specify any billing period.

Select the billing start date

Recurring payments can be started immediately when you create a subscription or with a delay.

Example: a customer subscribes to your service in the middle of the month, you create a monthly recurring payments plan that starts on the 15th of the next month.

Payment limit restrictions

You can specify the maximum amount of payments for a subscription or create a plan with no restrictions. In the former case, recurring payments will automatically stop once all payments in the billing schedule have been completed.

Example: a customer purchases a product worth 12,000 rubles under a one-year installment plan, pays 1,000 rubles as the initial payment, and subscribes to a recurring payment plan of 1,000 rubles per month for no more than 11 charges.

Plan suspension

A recurring payment subscription can be suspended for any period of time from the dashboard or via API.

Example: a customer requests to pause the service for a couple of months, so you push back the next payment date by the corresponding period. _Recurrent

Payment amount customization

Initial payment amount

The initial payment amount can be flexible and may differ from the amount of subsequent recurring payments.

Example: when a customer registers for your service, you ask them to make a setup payment of 1 ruble to verify the card. Afterward, with the user's consent, you can start recurring payments for any amount.

Recurring payment amount

The recurring payment amount can be changed at any point during the subscription plan lifecycle from the dashboard or via the API.

Example: you provide the customer with a discount for the first 2 months of using the service, and then increase the subscription amount. _Recurrent

Automated error resolution

Errors that occur during recurring payment execution can be divided into: recoverable and unrecoverable.

The first category includes errors related to a lack of funds on the customer's card, temporary technical issues, or unavailability of the card issuer. As a rule, these problems can be resolved by the cardholder.

The second category covers errors that cannot be fixed, such as an expired card, a lost card, or a revoked license of the issuing bank.

Depending on the category, the system responds to and processes recurring payment errors differently.

Interaction with the cardholder

If the card is declined due to insufficient funds, the system notifies the cardholder that the scheduled payment failed, recommends topping up the card balance, and informs them that a retry attempt will be made the following day.

Retry attempts

The system retries the card charges for several consecutive days if a scheduled payment fails due to a recoverable error.

Card update

The system prompts the user to enter new card details via its interface to resume recurring payments. If the customer agrees, the system executes a new initial payment using the updated card details, credits the payment to the subscription and continues to process recurring payments using the new card.

Customer notification

An important function of recurring payments is to timely inform the cardholder about the upcoming scheduled payment date. Some customers can be forgetful, so a warning about an upcoming payment eliminates the element of surprise and significantly reduces the likelihood of insufficient funds on the card. CloudPayments always reminds payers of the date of the next payment, specifying the amount, purpose, and the recipient of the payment.

The second category covers errors that cannot be fixed, such as an expired card, a lost card, or a revoked license of the issuing bank.

Depending on the category, the system responds to and processes recurring payment errors differently.

If the card is declined due to insufficient funds, the system notifies the cardholder that the scheduled payment failed, recommends topping up the card balance, and informs them that a retry attempt will be made the following day.
The system retries the card charges for several consecutive days if a scheduled payment fails due to a recoverable error.

The system prompts the user to enter new card details via its interface to resume recurring payments. If the customer agrees, the system executes a new initial payment using the updated card details, credits the payment to the subscription and continues to process recurring payments using the new card.

An important function of recurring payments is to timely inform the cardholder about the upcoming scheduled payment date. Some customers can be forgetful, so a warning about an upcoming payment eliminates the element of surprise and significantly reduces the likelihood of insufficient funds on the card. CloudPayments always reminds payers of the date of the next payment, specifying the amount, purpose, and the recipient of the payment.

content.text: Recurring payments, also known as subscription payments or automated payments, let you charge the customer's bank card regularly without requiring the payer to re-enter card details or initiate each payment.

Recurring payments always start with the initial payment, for which the payer must enter the details of his card. For subsequent recurring payments, you must familiarize the cardholder with the billing schedule and obtain their consent for direct debiting.

There is a common belief that recurring billing simply boils down to setting an amount to be charged to the customer's card each month. Consequently, the choice of a recurring payment provider is often based solely on the cost of the services. In reality, the process is more complex, because quality service requires far more features and capabilities. We have done everything to make launching and processing recurring payments in CloudPayments as simple and flexible as possible.

Recurring payments can be started at any time after the initial payment: immediately, one week later, or one month later. There is only one restriction: the interval between recurring payments, as well as between the initial payment and the first recurring payment, cannot exceed one year.
the customer pays for the first month of service through an initial payment and agrees to monthly debiting from their card starting from the second month.
Recurring payments can be started via API or payment widget.
If the customer cancels further payments, you can terminate the subscription at any time:
Additionally, the payer can independently find and cancel their recurring payments on the CloudPayments website:
Select the billing period and interval
The system can make recurring payments every 2 weeks, once a month, every 3 months, and so on: you can specify any billing period.
Recurring payments can be started immediately when you create a subscription or with a delay.
a customer subscribes to your service in the middle of the month, you create a monthly recurring payments plan that starts on the 15th of the next month.

You can specify the maximum amount of payments for a subscription or create a plan with no restrictions. In the former case, recurring payments will automatically stop once all payments in the billing schedule have been completed.

a customer purchases a product worth 12,000 rubles under a one-year installment plan, pays 1,000 rubles as the initial payment, and subscribes to a recurring payment plan of 1,000 rubles per month for no more than 11 charges.

bezopasnaya-sdelka.title: Escrow service
bezopasnaya-sdelka.html:
Product description

The Escrow service enables settlement processing between two individuals for the sale of goods or services. In this case, interaction between individuals does not happen directly, but rather through the Platform, a legal entity that facilitates the listing of the Product on its storefront, helps the Seller find a buyer, and organizes dispute resolution when necessary. The Platform monitors the transaction progress and instructs CloudPayments to charge the buyer's card at the time of purchase. Once the seller successfully fulfills their obligations (for example, upon completion of the agreed services or works, or successful delivery of the product), the Platform initiates the payout to the seller's card.

Definitions and terms

  • Payer: an individual who sends money.

  • Recipient: an individual who receives money.

  • Platform: an intermediary that acts as a guarantor of the security of the transaction and determines whether the parties have fulfilled their obligations. In case of disputes, it acts as an Arbitrator and bears financial liability.

  • Transaction is the process of acquiring goods/services from one individual to another.

  • Payment: the purchase of goods or services from an individual.

  • Payout: the receipt of remuneration by an individual who has provided a service or sold a product.

  • Widget: a pop-up form used to enter the payer's card details and email address.

  • Checkout: a script embedded into a website that collects card details from a specified form and uses them to generate a cryptogram for payment processing via the API.

  • AccumulationId: a unique transaction ID assigned during the initial transaction.

  • TransactionId: a unique transaction ID.

Connection setup

To enable the Escrow service, you must submit a request to your account manager or specify this during the onboarding phase with your assigned manager.

Warning: Operating via Escrow requires setting up 2 terminals: one for processing payments and another for processing payouts.

Warning: Escrow payments and payouts are available exclusively via bank card or a token generated during a card payment. Escrow is not supported for any other payment methods, including international card payments.

Also, please note that not all acquiring banks connected to CloudPayments support the Escrow service. Please contact your account manager for details.

Workflows

  1. Accumulating several payments and making a single payout (N:1)

  2. Splitting a single payment into multiple payouts (1:N)

Escrow status model


N:1

Widget integration diagram

The variable specifying the transaction type is located within the cp.constant.escrow object. It determines the escrow workflow:

  1. Multiple payments to a single payout

  2. A single payment to multiple payouts

javascript
{
  NToOne: 0,  // For N:1 workflow
  OneToN: 1   // For 1:N workflow
}

If this variable is omitted, the system automatically defaults to the N:1 transaction protocol.

Example:

javascript
cp.constant.escrow.NToOne // Transaction type variable = 0
cp.constant.escrow.OneToN // Transaction type variable = 1


Payment (initial accumulation)

javascript
var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();

const intentParams = {
  publicTerminalId: "test_api_00000000000000000000002",
  paymentSchema: 'Dual',
  description: Payment for order #...",
  amount: 100,
  currency: "RUB",
  culture: "ru-RU",
  skin: "classic",
  externalId: 'string',
  receiptEmail: "user@email.com",
  userInfo: {
    email: "user@email.com",
    phone: "+71234567890",
  },
  metadata: {
    myProp: "myProp value",
  },
  escrow: {
    startAccumulation: true,
    accumulationId: null,
    escrowType: "NToOne"
  },
};

widget.oncomplete = (result) => {
  console.log(result);
}

widget.start(intentParams).then(function(widgetResult) {
  console.log('result', widgetResult); // Success callback
}).catch(function(error) {
  console.log('error', error); // Error callback
});

In response to the request, a unique EscrowAccumulationId ID will be received within the Pay notification.

Also, if the transaction is successful, the EscrowAccumulationId will be included in all webhooks except for the Check webhook.

Payment (for an active accumulation)

For subsequent requests (payments) within the created escrow transaction, fields accumulationId, startAccumulation, escrowType must be added to the escrow object.

    accumulationId: "4733183a-c6f6-4c1b-8ff1-fb7c43ed1695" // Payment for accumulation already created
}

Checkout API integration workflow

Payout

To complete the transaction, you must send the request to the payments/token/topup endpoint, specifying the AccumulationId ID and the array of transactions to be paid out:

text
"Escrow": {
  "AccumulationId": "365b6942-94e8-4c5b-aff5-392dc1a51c28",
  "TransactionIds": [10649405, 10649404],
  "EscrowType": "NToOne"
}

The array of payment transactions for the payout must contain only transactions processed through the payment terminal associated with the current AccumulationId ID.

Payouts will be made only for the TransactionId values that have been specified in the TransactionIds array in the payments/token/topup request.

It is not possible to process payouts for the omitted transactions, as the transaction will already be closed. Therefore it is impossible to perform either a payment or a payout against a closed escrow transaction.

Warning: Any payment transactions that were not submitted for escrow closure will be automatically refunded to the payer.

Restrictions

The payout amount must be less than or equal to the total payment amount.

None of the transactions specified in the payout array must have any cancellations or full refunds (partial refunds are allowed).

If a payment request is sent with an AccumulationId for which a payout has already been processed, the payment will be declined.

All transactions submitted for a payout must:

  • Share the same AccumulationId

  • Be unpaid

  • Be in the RUB currency

  • Be of the Payment type

  • Be in the Completed status

Payout

To complete the transaction, you must send the request to the payments/token/topup endpoint, specifying the AccumulationId ID and an array of transactions to be paid out. The array should contain only one TransactionId, according to the escrow workflow:

javascript
"Escrow": {
  "AccumulationId": "365b6942-94e8-4c5b-aff5-392dc1a51c28",
  "TransactionIds": [10649404],
  "EscrowType": "OneToN"
}

Warning: Payouts can be processed until the sum of all payouts equals the total escrow transaction amount.

There are two methods for closing an escrow transaction:

1. Pass "FinalPayout": true within the Escrow object.

This closes the escrow transaction even if the total payout amount is less than the original payment amount.

javascript
"Escrow": {
  "AccumulationId": "365b6942-94e8-4c5b-aff5-392dc1a51c28",
  "TransactionIds": [10649404],
  "EscrowType": "OneToN",
  "FinalPayout": true
}

2. When the sum of all payouts equals the original payment amount, the escrow transaction will be closed automatically.

Payments will be made only for the TransactionId specified in the TransactionIds array in the payments/token/topup request. For the 1:N workflow, this array must contain only a single payment transaction ID.

Restrictions

The payout amount must be less than or equal to the total payment amount.

The payment transaction must not have any cancellations or full refunds (partial refunds are allowed).

All transactions submitted for a payout must:

  • Share the same AccumulationId

  • Be in the RUB currency

  • Be in the Completed status

  • Be processed within a single workflow (OneToN)

  • Belong to an escrow transaction that has not been closed — "FinalPayout": true must not have been passed, and the total payout amount must be less than the original payment amount

Retrieve transaction status by AccumulationId

To retrieve information, you must send an HTTP request with the Basic Auth authorization type.

Use the terminal's public key (PK) as the username. Both the payment and payout terminals can be used.

The password is the API secret associated with that specific PK.

Notice: The PK and API secret can be found in the dashboard under the website settings.

Warning: Information retrieval is only available for the AccumulationId values generated within this specific pair of terminals.

  • An array of unpaid payments:

    • Payments transaction ID

    • Transaction status

    • Transaction amount

  • An array of paid-out payments:

    • Payments transaction ID

    • Transaction status

    • Transaction amount

  • An array of refunds for all transactions:

    • Payments transaction ID

    • Transaction status

    • Transaction amount

  • An array of payout transactions for the 1:N workflow:

    • Payout transaction ID

    • Transaction status

    • Payout transaction amount

    • The IsFinalPayout escrow closure flag

  • Balance:

    • Balance = PaymentsSum - RefundsSum - PayoutsSum

The array of payment transactions for the payout must contain only transactions processed through the payment terminal associated with the current AccumulationId ID.

Payouts will be made only for the TransactionId values that have been specified in the TransactionIds array in the payments/token/topup request.

It is not possible to process payouts for the omitted transactions, as the transaction will already be closed. Therefore it is impossible to perform either a payment or a payout against a closed escrow transaction.

None of the transactions specified in the payout array must have any cancellations or full refunds (partial refunds are allowed).

Warning: Payouts can be processed until the sum of all payouts equals the total escrow transaction amount.

There are two methods for closing an escrow transaction:

1. Pass "FinalPayout": true within the Escrow object.

This closes the escrow transaction even if the total payout amount is less than the original payment amount.

javascript
"Escrow": {
  "AccumulationId": "365b6942-94e8-4c5b-aff5-392dc1a51c28",
  "TransactionIds": [10649404],
  "EscrowType": "OneToN",
  "FinalPayout": true
}

2. When the sum of all payouts equals the original payment amount, the escrow transaction will be closed automatically.

Payments will be made only for the TransactionId specified in the TransactionIds array in the payments/token/topup request. For the 1:N workflow, this array must contain only a single payment transaction ID.

The payout amount must be less than or equal to the total payment amount.

The payment transaction must not have any cancellations or full refunds (partial refunds are allowed).

All transactions submitted for a payout must:

  • Share the same AccumulationId

  • Be in the RUB currency

  • Be in the Completed status

  • Be processed within a single workflow (OneToN)

  • Belong to an escrow transaction that has not been closed — "FinalPayout": true must not have been passed, and the total payout amount must be less than the original payment amount

To retrieve information, you must send an HTTP request with the Basic Auth authorization type.

Use the terminal's public key (PK) as the username. Both the payment and payout terminals can be used.

The password is the API secret associated with that specific PK.

Notice: The PK and API secret can be found in the dashboard under the website settings.

Warning: Information retrieval is only available for the AccumulationId values generated within this specific pair of terminals.

    • Payout transaction ID

content.text: The Escrow service enables settlement processing between two individuals for the sale of goods or services. In this case, interaction between individuals does not happen directly, but rather through the Platform, a legal entity that facilitates the listing of the Product on its storefront, helps the Seller find a buyer, and organizes dispute resolution when necessary. The Platform monitors the transaction progress and instructs CloudPayments to charge the buyer's card at the time of purchase. Once the seller successfully fulfills their obligations (for example, upon completion of the agreed services or works, or successful delivery of the product), the Platform initiates the payout to the seller's card.

: an intermediary that acts as a guarantor of the security of the transaction and determines whether the parties have fulfilled their obligations. In case of disputes, it acts as an Arbitrator and bears financial liability.

SDK-dlya-Android.title: Android SDK
SDK-dlya-Android.html:
The SDK allows you to integrate payment acceptance into a mobile app for the Android platform.

The main version is available on GitHub.

The app explains how to obtain card details, generate a cryptogram, perform 3D Secure authorization, and make a payment on an Android device. SDK Android

Terms of use

  • If you need to route data through your own server, you do not need PCI DSS certification. The card data is sent in encrypted form, and the decryption keys are only available in the CloudPayments payment gateway. They are not included in the app or library.

  • Card details can be entered via keyboard or scanned using a service such as card.io. Never save or log the full card number or CVV.

  • Do not use mobile SDK for mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) terminals. The SDK is intended for apps installed on the phones and tablets of your customers.

  • According to the Google Play rules, mobile app developers are allowed to accept payments through third-party payment systems only when selling non-digital products or digital products that can be used outside of the app.

The SDK lets you integrate payment acceptance into iOS mobile apps.

Main version can be found on GitHub.

The app will guide you through obtaining card data, generating a cryptogram, performing 3D Secure authentication, and processing a payment on an iPhone or iPad. SDK Ios.

Terms of use

  • If you need to route data through your own server, you do not need PCI DSS certification. The card data is sent in encrypted form, and the decryption keys are available only in the CloudPayments payment gateway. They are not included in the app or library.

  • Card details can be entered via keyboard or scanned using a service such as card.io. Never save or write to logs the full card number or CVV.

  • According to the App Store rules, mobile app developers are allowed to receive payments using external payment systems only when selling non-digital goods or digital products that can be used outside of the app.

api.title: API.
api.html:
API is the system application programming interface for interacting with merchant platforms.

The interface is available at api.cloudpayments.ru and supports features for executing payments, canceling payments, issuing refunds, capturing two-stage payments, creating and canceling subscriptions for recurring payments, and sending invoices via email.

How it works

  • Parameters are sent via the POST method either as key=value pairs in the request body or in JSON format.

  • The API can accept no more than 150,000 fields per single request. API response timeout: 5 minutes.

  • In all requests to the API, if you pass a floating-point number into an integer field, the API does not return an error; instead, mathematical rounding will be applied automatically.

  • The API limits the maximum number of concurrent requests to 5 for test terminals and to 30 for production terminals. If the number of requests currently processed exceeds the limit, the API returns a 429 HTTP status code (Too Many Requests) until at least one request has finished processing. If you need to revise these limits, contact your account manager.

The choice of parameter transmission format is determined on the client side and controlled through the Content-Type request header.

  • For key=value parameters, use Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

  • For JSON parameters, use Content-Type: application/json.

The system returns a JSON response containing at least the following two parameters: Success and Message:

javascript
{ "Success": false, "Message": "Invalid Amount value" }

Request authentication

To authenticate a request, HTTP Basic Auth is used to send the username and password within the HTTP request header. The Public ID is used as the username, and the API Secret is used as the password. Both values can be obtained from the dashboard.

Warning: If the request does not include an authentication header or contains incorrect authentication data, the system returns a 401 HTTP status (Unauthorized).

Notice: The API Secret is used for security. It must be stored in a secure location.

API idempotency

Idempotency is an API property that ensures that a repeated request returns the same result as the initial request without being processed again. This means that you can send multiple requests to a system with the same ID, only one successful request will be processed, and all responses will be identical. This mechanism protects against network errors that could otherwise result in duplicate records or actions.

To enable idempotency, pass the X-Request-ID header containing a unique ID in your API request. You generate this request ID. It can be a GUID, a combination of the order number, date, and amount, or any other value at your discretion.

Each new request that requires processing must include a unique X-Request-ID value. The processed result is retained in the system for 1 hour.

Test method

Use the test method to verify your connection to the API.

Endpoint:

https://api.cloudpayments.ru/test

Request parameters:

None

Example response:

The method returns the request status in the response.

{"Success":true,"Message":"bd6353c3-0ed6-4a65-946f-083664bf8dbd"}

The phone number must be passed in the Phone parameter within the Payer object.

Any other data associated with the transaction, including instructions for creating a subscription or generating an online receipt, must be wrapped in the cloudpayments object.

The server returns a JSON file with three components: the success field (the result of the request), the message field (a description of the error), and the model object (extended information).

Possible options

  • Malformed request:

    • Success: false

    • Message: error description

  • Transaction declined:

    • Success: false

    • Model: transaction information and an error code

  • Transactions accepted:

    • Success: true

    • Model: transaction information

Notice: The request result (the Success field) does not reflect the transaction status; it only indicates the success or failure of the API request. The transaction status is reflected in the additional Status field, and can also be obtained via received notifications.

API is the system application programming interface for interacting with merchant platforms.

The interface is available at api.cloudpayments.ru and supports features for executing payments, canceling payments, issuing refunds, capturing two-stage payments, creating and canceling subscriptions for recurring payments, and sending invoices via email.

• Parameters are sent via the POST method either as key=value pairs in the request body or in JSON format.

  • The API can accept no more than 150,000 fields per single request. API response timeout: 5 minutes.

  • In all requests to the API, if you pass a floating-point number into an integer field, the API does not return an error; instead, mathematical rounding will be applied automatically.

  • The API limits the maximum number of concurrent requests to 5 for test terminals and to 30 for production terminals. If the number of requests currently processed exceeds the limit, the API returns a 429 HTTP status code (Too Many Requests) until at least one request has finished processing. If you need to revise these limits, contact your account manager.

The choice of parameter transmission format is determined on the client side and controlled through the Content-Type request header.

  • For key=value parameters, use Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

  • For JSON parameters, use Content-Type: application/json.

The system returns a JSON response containing at least the following two parameters: Success and Message:

javascript
{ "Success": false, "Message": "Invalid Amount value" }

To authenticate a request, HTTP Basic Auth is used to send the username and password within the HTTP request header. The Public ID is used as the username, and the API Secret is used as the password. Both values can be obtained from the dashboard.

Warning: If the request does not include an authentication header or contains incorrect authentication data, the system returns a 401 HTTP status (Unauthorized).

Notice: The API Secret is used for security. It must be stored in a secure location.

Idempotency is an API property that ensures that a repeated request returns the same result as the initial request without being processed again. This means that you can send multiple requests to a system with the same ID, only one successful request will be processed, and all responses will be identical. This mechanism protects against network errors that could otherwise result in duplicate records or actions.

To enable idempotency, pass the X-Request-ID header containing a unique ID in your API request. You generate this request ID. It can be a GUID, a combination of the order number, date, and amount, or any other value at your discretion.

Each new request that requires processing must include a unique X-Request-ID value. The processed result is retained in the system for 1 hour.

Use the test method to verify your connection to the API.

https://api.cloudpayments.ru/test

Request parameters:

None

Example response:

Notice: According to the NSPK requirements, merchant platforms providing telecommunication services (MCC 4814 Telecommunication Services), must provide the payer's phone number. If the phone number is missing from the request, acquiring banks will decline the transactions.

The phone number must be passed in the Phone parameter within the Payer object.

Format: digits only, without delimiters such as hyphens, or parentheses.

Example: "+71234567890"

uvedomleniya.title: Notifications
uvedomleniya.html:
A notification is an HTTP request from the system to your website. Such requests are also called callback or webhook. The system supports several types of notifications: for checking whether a payment can be processed, for informing about successful and failed payments, for notifying about changes to recurring payment subscriptions, and for informing about issued receipts.

Warning: Activation and deactivation of notifications, as well as adjustment of addresses and formats of notifications are carried out in the dashboard.

Notice: If you are using notifications to verify and change order status in your system, we recommend checking the amount, order number, and account ID of the payer.

Notice: The following rule applies to notifications (Pay, Fail, Recurrent, Cancel, Confirm, Refund): if the system cannot connect to the merchant's server, or receives an incorrect response, or a response with a code other than zero, it will make 100 attempts to deliver the message. The intervals between retries, in minutes, are as follows: 1, 2, 5, 10, 30. Response timeout: 30 seconds. In less than 1% of cases, the delay may reach 2 minutes. In other cases, it is less than a second. _Notifications

Check

Verify notifications

All notification types (Check, Pay, Fail, Confirm, Cancel, Refund, and Recurrent) include two HTTP headers: X-Content-HMAC and Content-HMAC. These headers contain a request verification value calculated using the HMAC algorithm. The only difference between them is that the first one is generated from URL-decoded (or non-encoded) parameters, and the second one is generated from the URL-encoded parameters, which can sometimes cause processing issues. If you need to verify the authenticity and integrity of your notifications, you can calculate the verification value on your side and compare it with the value received in the request. A match confirms that the notification was sent by us and arrived in its original form.

When implementing message verification, please consider the following details:

  • For notifications sent via the POST method, the message is the request body. For GET requests, the message is the query string.

  • The UTF8 encoding must be used when calculating the HMAC.

  • The hash is calculated using the SHA256 function.

  • The API Secret (available in the dashboard) must be used as the key.

  • The calculated value is passed in base64 encoding.

Examples of calculating HMAC in different programming languages are available at the link provided in the source.

The IP addresses from which the system sends notifications are 185.98.81.0/28, 87.251.91.160/27, 46.46.175.96/27, 46.46.168.160/27, 162.55.174.97/32, and 91.216.178.243/32.

Warning: In accordance with global security trends and identified vulnerabilities, support for the SSL 3.0 protocol has been discontinued. Support ended on June 8, 2020.

For you, this means the following:

  • If you do not use Pay, Check, Fail, Confirm, Refund, Recurrent, or Cancel notifications, no action is required.

  • If you use at least one of these notifications, you must check which HTTPS encryption protocols your server supports. If your server only supports SSL 3.0, you must upgrade it to at least TLS 1.1. Upgrading to TLS 1.3 is highly recommended. As a last resort, you can switch your notifications to the HTTP protocol.

For more details, see How to disable SSL 3.0.

After June 8, HTTPS notifications to servers that support only SSL 3.0 may fail to deliver.

A notification is an HTTP request from the system to your website. Such requests are also called callback or webhook. The system supports several types of notifications: for checking whether a payment can be processed, for informing about successful and failed payments, for notifying about changes to recurring payment subscriptions, and for informing about issued receipts.

Warning: Activation and deactivation of notifications, as well as adjustment of addresses and formats of notifications are carried out in the dashboard.

Notice: If you are using notifications to verify and change order status in your system, we recommend checking the amount, order number, and account ID of the payer.

Notice: The following rule applies to notifications (Pay, Fail, Recurrent, Cancel, Confirm, Refund): if the system cannot connect to the merchant's server, or receives an incorrect response, or a response with a code other than zero, it will make 100 attempts to deliver the message. The intervals between retries, in minutes, are as follows: 1, 2, 5, 10, 30. Response timeout: 30 seconds. In less than 1% of cases, the delay may reach 2 minutes. In other cases, it is less than a second. _Notifications

All notification types (Check, Pay, Fail, Confirm, Cancel, Refund, and Recurrent) include two HTTP headers: X-Content-HMAC and Content-HMAC. These headers contain a request verification value calculated using the HMAC algorithm. The only difference between them is that the first one is generated from URL-decoded (or non-encoded) parameters, and the second one is generated from the URL-encoded parameters, which can sometimes cause processing issues. If you need to verify the authenticity and integrity of your notifications, you can calculate the verification value on your side and compare it with the value received in the request. A match confirms that the notification was sent by us and arrived in its original form.

When implementing message verification, please consider the following details:

  • For notifications sent via the POST method, the message is the request body. For GET requests, the message is the query string.

  • The UTF8 encoding must be used when calculating the HMAC.

  • The hash is calculated using the SHA256 function.

  • The API Secret (available in the dashboard) must be used as the key.

  • The calculated value is passed in base64 encoding.

Examples of calculating HMAC in different programming languages are available at the link provided in the source.

The IP addresses from which the system sends notifications are 185.98.81.0/28, 87.251.91.160/27, 46.46.175.96/27, 46.46.168.160/27, 162.55.174.97/32, and 91.216.178.243/32.

Warning: In accordance with global security trends and identified vulnerabilities, support for the SSL 3.0 protocol has been discontinued. Support ended on June 8, 2020.

For you, this means the following:

  • If you do not use Pay, Check, Fail, Confirm, Refund, Recurrent, or Cancel notifications, no action is required.

  • If you use at least one of these notifications, you must check which HTTPS encryption protocols your server supports. If your server only supports SSL 3.0, you must upgrade it to at least TLS 1.1. Upgrading to TLS 1.3 is highly recommended. As a last resort, you can switch your notifications to the HTTP protocol.

For more details, see How to disable SSL 3.0.

After June 8, HTTPS notifications to servers that support only SSL 3.0 may fail to deliver.

t-pay.title: T-Pay
t-pay.html:
CloudPayments offers a one-click payment method through T-Pay. The customer can choose any payment account in the T-Bank app, as well as earn T-Bank cashback for future purchases.

T-Pay payments can be accepted through the SDK. You can implement this either through the CloudPayments payment form or as a separate button.

See the documentation for more details:

  • SDK for iOS

  • SDK for Android

Get a payment link

Description

Method for getting the payment link to redirect the customer to the bank’s mobile app.

The response will return the QrUrl parameter with the redirect URL.

To process the payment, redirect the customer to the received URL.

Endpoint

https://api.cloudpayments.ru/payments/qr/tinkoffpay/link

Request parameters

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

publicId

string

Yes

Website ID, can be found in the dashboard

Amount

decimal

Yes

The payment amount in the transaction currency. Use a dot as the decimal separator. Number of decimal places: 2

Currency

string

Yes

Currency: RUB (see the reference)

Scheme

enum string

Yes

Payment processing method (see Transaction types). Possible values: 0 for single-stage payment, 1 for two-stage payment

Browser

string

Yes

Customer's browser name derived from the browser's User-Agent string. Example values: Chrome, Firefox, MIUI Browser, Opera

Os

string

Yes

Payer's device operating system. Example values: Android, iOS, Windows

Webview

bool

Yes

Indicator of whether the browser is running in WebView mode. Possible values: true for payments using webview, false for payments without webview

Device

enum string

Yes

Payer's device type flag. Possible values: MobileApp for payments initiated from a mobile app, DesktopWeb for payments initiated from a desktop browser, Mobile for payments initiated from a mobile browser

SuccessRedirectUrl

string

Yes

Customer redirect URL after a successful payment. Once the payment is processed, the customer will be redirected from the bank's mobile app to the specified URL

FailRedirectUrl

string

Yes

URL for redirecting the customer after a failed payment. Once the payment is processed, the customer will be redirected from the bank's mobile app to the specified URL

IpAddress

string

No

Payer IP address

AccountId

string

No

User ID

Email

string

No

Payer email

InvoiceId

string

No

Invoice or order number

Description

string

No

Payment description (free-form)

JsonData

JSON

No

Any other data associated with the transaction, including instructions for creating a subscription or generating an online receipt, must be wrapped in the cloudpayments object. We have reserved the names of the following parameters and their values are displayed in the transaction register downloaded from the dashboard: name, firstName, middleName, lastName, nick, phone, address, comment, birthDate

TtlMinutes

int

No

Time window during which the payment via QR code or payment link remains available. If this parameter is omitted, the payment can be completed within 24 hours. Important: 0 is considered incorrect and may lead to a request processing error. If the time limit is not required, either do not pass this parameter or explicitly set it to null

SaveCard

bool

No

Flag indicating whether to save the card token for payments via a stored card. Possible values: true: after a successful payment, the card token will be returned, false: the token will not be returned (default). The SaveCard parameter is only processed when the "Save a card token" setting is enabled in the dashboard. If the "Force Save" setting is enabled, the SaveCard parameter will be ignored

The server returns a JSON response with the following three properties:

  • Success: request result

  • Message: error description

  • Model: additional information

Response examples:

  1. Malformed request:

    • Success: false

    • Message: error description

  2. Transaction declined:

    • Success: false

    • Model: transaction information and an error code

  3. Transaction accepted:

    • Success: true

    • Model: transaction information

Notice: The request result (the Success field) does not reflect the transaction status; it only indicates the success or failure of the API request. The transaction status is reflected in the additional Status field, and can also be obtained via received notifications. For the interpretation of transaction statuses, see reference.


Request example

javascript
{
    "Amount": "10",
    "AccountId": "someId",
    "InvoiceId": 12345,
    "Browser": "Chrome",
    "Currency": "RUB",
    "Device": "Mobile",
    "Description": "Payment with T-Pay",
    "Email": "email@email.com",
    "IpAddress": "123.123.123.123",
    "Os": "Android",
    "Scheme": 1,
    "TtlMinutes": 30,
    "SuccessRedirectUrl": "https://cp.ru",
    "FailRedirectUrl": "https://cp.ru",
    "Webview": false
}

Response example

javascript
{
    "Model": {
        "QrUrl": "{URL-address}",
        "QrImage": null,
        "TransactionId": 11122233344,
        "MerchantOrderId": "12345",
        "ProviderQrId": "",
        "Amount": 10,
        "Message": "Created",
        "IsTest": false
    },
    "Success": true,
    "Message": null
}

Description

Method for getting the QR code to show the customer in the browser.

Response will return the QrImage parameter containing a QR code in imageSVG format for displaying to the customer. The string value is Base64-encoded.

Endpoint

Request example

Response example

javascript
{
    "Model": {
        "QrUrl": null,
        "QrImage": "{string}",
        "TransactionId": 11122233344,
        "MerchantOrderId": "12345",
        "ProviderQrId": "",
        "Amount": 10,
        "Message": "Created",
        "IsTest": false
    },
    "Success": true,
    "Message": null
}

Refund

The refund method for SBP operations is identical to the refund method used for online acquiring operations. See API, Refund.

SBP refunds operate asynchronously. The final SBP refund status ("Completed" or "Declined") can be obtained via a Refund notification after the refund transaction has been created, rather than within the immediate response to the refund request itself.

Notifications for SBP operations are identical to notifications for internet acquiring operations. See Notifications.

The parameter responsible for the operation type within the notification is PaymentMethod (which is set to Sbp for SBP transactions).

If Check notifications are enabled, a Check request will be sent prior to generating the QR code or payment link to validate the data accuracy.

Generate direct links and the bank list

A direct link redirects the payer to a specific bank's mobile app when clicked.

The bank list can be retrieved from the array of elements returned in the response to the request POST: /sbp/v2/banks/info in the Model.Members parameter.

CloudPayments utilizes the participant list retrieved from the SBP widget API.

SBP integration requirements

Must remain unchanged:

  1. Bank order: the original sequence of banks must not be altered (the original order is maintained by CloudPayments)

  2. Names and logos

  3. URLs used to redirect customers to banking applications

Required:

  1. Bank search feature (must be preserved)

  2. Data caching (enforced on the CloudPayments side):

    • Use only data that is no more than 24 hours old

    • In the event of a request failure, use the latest available working data

Allowed customization:

  • Display the top 3 banks previously selected by the customer

Specifications of SBP bank list display

List element ordering

  1. Elements on the bank selection page must be arranged strictly in the order returned in the response to the POST /sbp/v2/banks/info request.

  2. Exception:

    • A maximum of 3 previously selected banks may be displayed at the top of the list.

    • The remaining banks must follow in their original sequence, excluding those already moved to the top.

Bank logo

The bank logo must be retrieved from the response to the POST /sbp/v2/banks/info request, using the Model.Members.logo parameter.

Bank name

The bank name must be retrieved from the response to the POST /sbp/v2/banks/info request, using the Model.Members.Name parameter.

Link to the bank app

To generate a direct link that redirects the customer to a specific bank's mobile application, use the following steps:

  1. Retrieve the payment link from the response to the POST /payments/qr/sbp/link request, using the Model.QrUrl parameter.

  2. Retrieve the bank link template from the response to the POST /sbp/v2/banks/info request, using the Model.Members.url parameter.

  3. Process the link template:

    • Remove the trailing path element: {QRC_ID}{QUERY_STRING}.

  4. Generate the final link:

    • Concatenate the remaining part of the template with the path and query parameters extracted from the payment link.

URL transformation example

  1. Payment link: https://qr.nspk.ru/AD1000XXXXX1000?type=02&bank=100000000004&sum=1299900&cur=RUB&crc=8DA8

  2. Link template: https://online.vtb.ru/i/paymentSbp/{QRC_ID}{QUERY_STRING}

  3. Resulting link: https://online.vtb.ru/i/paymentSbp/AD1000XXXXX1000?type=02&bank=100000000004&sum=1299900&cur=RUB&crc=8DA8

digital-ruble.title: Digital ruble
digital-ruble.html:
Accepting digital rubles starting September 1, 2026

The digital ruble is a digital form of the Russian national currency issued by the Bank of Russia. It is equivalent to a cash ruble and is used for payments through the Bank of Russia's platform.

Who the requirements apply to

Starting September 1, 2026, merchants and service providers will be required to accept digital rubles if they meet all of the following criteria:

  • Generated revenue exceeding 120 million rubles in the previous year.

  • Use the services of a bank recognized as significant in the payment services market.

  • Accept payments from individuals.

How the requirements will be expanded

Starting September 1, 2027, the requirements will extend to companies with annual revenue exceeding 30 million rubles. Starting September 1, 2028, they will apply to all other merchants with annual revenue of at least 20 million rubles.

Who the requirements do not apply to

Companies with total annual revenue of less than 20 million rubles are not required to accept digital rubles.

The requirement also does not apply to:

  • Individual retail outlets with annual revenue of less than 5 million rubles, even if the company's total annual revenue exceeds 20 million rubles.

  • Points of sale without internet access.

Digital ruble support in CloudPayments

CloudPayments plans to start accepting one-time digital ruble payments on September 1, 2026. These transactions will be displayed within the dashboard and included in transaction registers and financial reporting.

Until the end of 2026, the fee for accepting digital ruble payments will be 0%. Recurring payments and saving payment details for subsequent payments will not be supported at launch.

How to connect

If you already accept payments via CloudPayments, contact your account manager or send a message to support via the chat in the dashboard.

If you do not yet work with CloudPayments, submit a request to connect.

Integration documentation will be provided to existing clients upon request and to new clients after they connect to CloudPayments.

This method does not require HTTP Basic Auth. Instead, the request uses the PublicId parameter in the request body to identify the terminal.

Endpoint

https://api.cloudpayments.ru/payments/qr/sberpay/link

Request parameters

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

string

Yes

Website ID, can be found in the dashboard

Amount

decimal

Yes

Payment amount in rubles. Use a dot as the decimal separator. Number of decimal places: 2

Currency

string

Yes

Currency: RUB (see currency list)

Description

string

No

Payment description (free-form)

AccountId

string

No

User ID, required to create a subscription and obtain a token

Email

string

No

Payer email for receiving payment confirmation

JsonData

JSON

No

Any other data associated with the transaction, including instructions for creating a subscription or generating an online receipt, must be wrapped in the cloudpayments object. We have reserved the names of the following parameters and their values are displayed in the transaction register downloaded from the dashboard: name, firstName, middleName, lastName, nick, phone, address, comment, birthDate

string

No

Scheme

enum string

Yes

Payment processing method (view Transaction types). Possible values: charge for single-stage payment; auth for two-stage payment

SuccessRedirectUrl

string

No

IpAddress

string

No

Payer IP address

Os

string

Yes

Payer's device operating system. Example values: Android, iOS, Windows

Webview

bool

Yes

Device

string

Yes

Payer's device type flag. Possible values: MobileApp for payments initiated from a mobile app; DesktopWeb for payments initiated from a desktop browser; Mobile for payments initiated from a mobile browser

Browser

string

Yes

Customer browser name based on browser userAgent. Example values: Chrome, Firefox, MIUI Browser, Opera

The server returns a JSON response with the following three properties:

  • Success: request result

  • Message: error description

  • Model: additional information

Response examples:

  1. Malformed request

    • Success: false

    • Message: error description

  2. Transaction declined:

    • Success: false

    • Model: transaction information and error code

  3. Transaction accepted:

    • Success: true

    • Model: transaction information

Notice: Request result from the Success field does not reflect transaction status; it only indicates the success or failure of the API request. Transaction status is reflected in the additional Status field, and can also be obtained via received notifications. For the interpretation of transaction statuses, see reference. _Sber Pay

    "Email": "email@email.com",
    "InvoiceId": "order_no4009",
    "Scheme": "charge",
    "SuccessRedirectUrl": "https://cp.ru"
}

        "QrImage": null,
        "TransactionId": 11122233344,
        "Amount": 10
    },
    "Success": true,
    "Message": null
}

mirpay.title: MIR Pay.
mirpay.html:
Mir Pay allows customers to pay for purchases with a single touch using Mir payment system cards. The Mir Pay button is displayed on the checkout page next to other payment methods.

Integration options

CloudPayments offers a simplified Mir Pay integration on the checkout page via the payment widget or the mobile SDK. No additional integration with the Mir payment system service is required.

In the near future, Mir Pay will become available for other integration options, including payment blocks, orders, and payment links.

Enable Mir Pay

To enable the Mir Pay button in the payment widget or the mobile SDK:

Enable the Mir Pay feature toggle in your website settings in the dashboard, or contact CloudPayments support.


Mir Pay payment process

  • After clicking the Pay button, the customer is redirected to the CloudPayments widget, where they can select Mir Pay without entering their card details.

  • After completing the payment, the customer sees a confirmation message and is automatically redirected back to the website. The merchant receives a transaction notification.

  • The merchant does not need to perform any custom integration with the Mir payment system service; all the required functionality is provided by CloudPayments.

dolyami.title: Dolyame
dolyami.html:
CloudPayments offers the Dolyame payment method. The user can split the payment into four parts, and the store receives the full amount on the next business day.

Integration methods

  • In the payment widget and CMS/CRM modules

  • In CloudInfoshop (storefront created from the dashboard)

  • In orders

  • In payment links generated in the dashboard

  • Via the API

Connection

To connect this payment method, contact your dedicated manager or write to the following email: assistant@cp.ru

For technical issues, contact support at support@cp.ru.

Embedded payment button

You can add a Dolyame payment button to your website. This method works through the CloudPayments public API and allows you to embed a separate payment button on your form.

The interface is available at api.cloudpayments.ru

Method POST /payments/altpay/pay

This method is used to obtain a payment link by submitting a Dolyame application.

There is no HTTP Basic Auth authentication for this method. Instead, the terminal ID parameter PublicId is used in the request body.
